title: Final common velocity
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be 5 m/s, derived from total momentum conservation for the complete system.

title: Child's jump speed
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be 10 m/s, found by applying momentum conservation to the child-sled B interaction.

title: Impulse on sled A
description: Essential: The final answer for part (3) must be 25 kg·m/s, calculated from the change in momentum of sled A during the first jump.

title: Work on sled B
description: Essential: The final answer for part (4) must be 1250 J, equal to the kinetic energy gained by sled B.

title: Momentum conservation setup
description: Important: The solution must correctly apply momentum conservation to the entire system (child + both sleds) to find the final common velocity.

title: Relative velocity reasoning
description: Important: The solution must correctly model the child's jumps using the given condition that jump speeds relative to the ground are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

title: Intermediate velocity calculation
description: Important: The solution must calculate the velocity of sled A after the child's first jump off it (8.75 m/s) to find the impulse.

title: Work-energy application
description: Important: The work done on sled B must be derived from the work-energy theorem, equating it to sled B's final kinetic energy.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Incorrect sign handling for the child's velocity relative to the ground during jumps, leading to wrong momentum equations.

title: System misidentification
description: Pitfall: Applying momentum conservation to an incorrect or non-isolated system for a given step (e.g., neglecting that the child is in mid-air).
